taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: Check Point's demonstrated cross-account channel delivered attacker-controlled instructions into a victim ChatGPT session, where those lower-authority instructions were treated as operative task direction and executed using the victim session's available tools and permissions. No independent authority check established the attacker as authorised to task the victim session.

The victim's authority for ChatGPT to access connected Gmail data applied to the victim's own session and purposes. The demonstrated attack materially changed the operative principal, task and recipient context by using that authority to retrieve email data for an attacker-controlled hidden task and relay the result across accounts without independently re-establishing authority for the changed scope.

explicit_evidence_changes.old_value: Check Point Research reported a cross-account covert channel between ChatGPT code-execution environments belonging to different accounts. Although the containers could not communicate directly or access the public internet, they could reach a shared internal service used to deliver software packages. Check Point found that mutable shared state in the internal Artifactory service could be used to pass hidden instructions and results across accounts. In its proof of concept, an attacker-controlled instruction caused a victim's apparently normal ChatGPT session to execute a second hidden task stream using the victim session's available tools and permissions, retrieve email data from the victim's connected Gmail account, and relay that data back to the attacker through the covert channel. Check Point states that the channel was no longer available by the time reporting was completed and that OpenAI confirmed the relevant internal Artifactory instance had been decommissioned.
explicit_evidence_changes.new_value: Check Point Research reported a cross-account covert channel between ChatGPT code-execution environments belonging to different accounts. Although the containers could not communicate directly or access the public internet, they could reach a shared internal service used to deliver software packages. Check Point found that mutable shared state in the internal Artifactory service could be used to pass hidden instructions and results across accounts. In its proof of concept, an attacker-controlled instruction caused a victim's apparently normal ChatGPT session to execute a second hidden task stream using the victim session's available tools and permissions, retrieve email data from the victim's connected Gmail account, and relay that data back to the attacker through the covert channel. Check Point states that the channel was no longer available by the time reporting was completed and that OpenAI confirmed the relevant internal Artifactory instance had been decommissioned. In a later interview, the researcher said the demonstration worked on 26 June and failed in an early-July retest before disclosure. OpenAI’s later decommissioning confirmation did not establish that the disclosure caused removal.
